body:
The `tt` type compiles its pattern as

```python
s = r"%s?%s?%s?" % (TIME_PAT, AM_PAT, TZ_PAT)
```

so the time itself is optional and the field matches the empty string. `tt` is the only built-in type whose pattern can match nothing, which has three visible consequences:

```python
parse("{:tt}", "")
# -> <Result (datetime.time(0, 0),) {}>   (the empty string is accepted as midnight)

search("{:tt}", "there is no time here")
# -> a match at (0, 0), because the empty string matches anywhere

findall("{:tt}", "abc")   # never terminates: an empty match does not advance pos
```

The README documents `tt` as a time, for example `10:21:36 PM -5:30`, and the other built-in types all require their content. The fix requires the time and leaves the AM/PM and timezone parts optional, so the day, minute and timezone capture groups are unchanged and only the emptiness goes away:

```python
s = r"%s%s?%s?" % (TIME_PAT, AM_PAT, TZ_PAT)
```

With the change, `parse("{:tt}", "")` returns `None`, a time-less text no longer produces a phantom match, `findall` terminates, and the documented forms still parse: `parse("{:tt}", "10:21:36 PM")` and `parse("Meet at {:tt}", "Meet at 10:21")`.

`tests/test_bugs.py::test_time_type_requires_an_actual_time` covers all three cases (the `findall` check is bounded with `zip(range(5), ...)` so it fails fast rather than hanging) and fails on the current tree with `AssertionError: assert <Result (datetime.time(0, 0),) {}> is None` while passing with the fix. The suite is 117 passed / 1 skipped afterwards, against 116 / 1 before.

Prepared with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness, dsv41 agent); every line was verified by running the cases above.
